text:
elaine: Heads-up — prepping answers for a customer's security questionnaire about tenant onboarding. Two asks: (1) full history of RBAC changes (who/what/when) exportable, and (2) chain-of-custody for audit logs + how we prove retention/immutability. Anyone have a short playbook or export commands I can paste?

matt: We keep RBAC change events in the config-audit table; service account rotations and policy diffs are logged too. For exports we produce signed snapshots. Short version: run the export job that produces a timestamped tar + GPG sig.

jia: +1. For the questionnaire wording we usually say: "RBAC change events are retained for 12 months by default and can be extended for enterprise contracts; exports include user, actor_id, change_blob, and a signed hash for integrity."

sam: If they need proof of no-tamper, we provide an audit bundle with an SHA256 manifest and our KMS-signed envelope. Example step:
```
# create export
./infra/tools/export_audit.sh --since 2023-01-01 --to s3://redwood-sec-exports/ACME/3240001234.tar.gz
# sign with KMS envelope
./infra/tools/sign_with_kms.sh s3://redwood-sec-exports/ACME/3240001234.tar.gz --key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/export-sign
```

matt: Also note: logs are forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk/Datadog depending on customer) and to a write-once S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled for customers who require WORM. Retention + Object Lock configuration is captured in the export metadata.

elaine: Great. Does anyone have the exact SQL for the RBAC audit table so I can show a sample row? They asked for column names.

jia: Sample: 
```
SELECT actor_id, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, diff, created_at, request_id
FROM config_audit.events
WHERE resource_type = 'rbac_policy' AND created_at >= '2024-01-01';
```

sam: If they ask about PII in logs — we redact principal emails in exports by default unless the contract requires full detail. Add that note.

elaine: Good call. Also: question about key provenance — they want to know if we use customer-managed keys or our KMS for signing audit exports.

matt: We support both. Default: Redwood-managed KMS for signatures. Enterprise: we can sign with customer-managed key (CMK) in their project/VPC or use HSM-backed key if on-prem. Document phrasing: "Customers may elect CMK signing for audit exports; Redwood will not retain plaintext customer keys."

deploy-bot: export job 3240001234 run by matt at 2024-11-14T16:02:10Z — uploaded s3://redwood-sec-exports/ACME/3240001234.tar.gz (sha256: d2f3...c1)

jia: Also add the incident response note: we maintain an immutable tamper-evident chain by storing manifests in an append-only ledger (audit-ledger table with insert-only writes). That, plus KMS signatures, is usually sufficient for enterprise auditors.

elaine: Perfect. Can someone paste a one-paragraph answer I can drop into the questionnaire?

sam: Draft: "Redwood captures RBAC changes and administrative actions in a config audit store (columns: actor_id, action, resource_type, diff, created_at, request_id). Events are retained for 12 months by default (extendable) and exports are produced as timestamped archives with an SHA256 manifest. Exports are signed using KMS; customers may require customer-managed keys for signatures. Audit logs are forwarded to SIEMs and may be exported to WORM-enabled S3 for tamper resistance. We also provide signed snapshots and an append-only audit ledger for chain-of-custody proofs."

elaine: This is excellent — I'll paste that and flag the CMK option. Thanks all :thumbsup:

matt: If Acme wants a live demo during their call, I can run the export and show the signature verification flow.

jia: I'll add a short FAQ blurb about redaction policy and how to request full detail under an NDA.

elaine: OK closing the loop — I'll attach the export sample and the signed manifest in the response. If they push for HSM-backed proofs, we'll escalate to infra for provisioning.

sam: FYI — ticket opened for customer CMK onboarding: INFRA-8672.

elaine: Thanks, everyone.
